name: Execute one kind of target
summary: A strike, usually at close range, that kills its target outright instead of dealing damage, so the target's health, armour and upgrades don't matter. It works only on one kind of target: soldiers for the attack dog and the commando's knife, non-robotic ground units for the brood spell, an enemy struck from behind, or one already worn down below a threshold. Anything else is out of reach (the dog can't bite a tank) or takes an ordinary hit. The attacker pays for that certainty: it usually has to get close (the brood spell, cast from range, is the exception), it tends to be fragile or slow to repeat, and in Red Alert only one attacker may go for each victim. It plays as a hunter of one kind of prey: the hunted kind stays together and shoots first, and every other kind can ignore it.
counterplay: Shoot it down on the approach: the hunter is usually fragile and must close in, so fast-firing small arms in a group stop it short, and a group of riflemen standing still is the worst place to send dogs.
Stay together: one hunter takes one victim at a time, and the victim's friends can kill it right after its strike, before it can try again.
Field the kinds it cannot touch: vehicles against the attack dog, robotic units against the brood spell.
Deny its condition: face the attacker so it can't get behind you, keep your health above the threshold, or carry gear that blocks one strike.
Kill the attacker before the strike lands: the brood spell does nothing if its caster dies while the shot is in flight, and killing an assassin mid-animation saves the victim.
Be immune for the moment: a target under an invulnerability effect takes nothing from a backstab (though some executes strip death-preventing buffs).

other_examples.note: The stealthed commando's knife kills one enemy soldier in reach at once, without breaking his stealth and without the victim's owner getting a unit-lost alert, so he can thin out sentries quietly. It is for infantry only: a Zero Hour patch fixed a bug that let the knife destroy aircraft. Stealth detection, mines and anti-infantry fire are what stop him.

An expensive spell, fired at range by a fragile flying caster, that destroys one targeted ground unit outright, however big (siege tanks and ultralisks are favourite victims), and hatches two short-lived broodlings from it. Robotic units, archons and spider mines can't be targeted, nor can anything in the air; if the caster dies while the shot is in flight, nothing happens. Massed air units and static defences keep the caster away.

sources.title: Spawn Broodling, Liquipedia StarCraft Brood War Wiki
Queen (StarCraft), StarCraft Wiki
sources.note: The page's spell box (transcluded from Template:SC1Broodling) gives the instant kill and the units it can't target; the prose gives the targets, the fragility and the counters.

other_examples.note: A short-reach ultimate: an enemy whose current health is at or below a threshold dies outright, and one above it just takes that much damage. A hero killed this way resets the cooldown and gives nearby allies a burst of speed and armour, and the strike strips several buffs that would otherwise stop the target from dying. The threshold version: any kind of target, but only once it is worn down.

sources.title: Axe, Liquipedia Dota 2 Wiki
sources.note: Read on Liquipedia because the Dota 2 Fandom wiki's Axe page gave the abilities other names than the game uses.

shooter_analogues.note: A knife hit on an enemy's back kills almost any player at once, whatever their health; the knife visibly raises when a stab is possible. Buildings and bosses can't be backstabbed, an invulnerable target takes nothing, and a Sniper item blocks one stab and briefly locks the Spy out of attacking. The positional version, where the condition is where you stand rather than what you hit.

A melee hit to an enemy's back kills instantly; holding the button instead plays a long third-person takedown. During that animation the attacker can be shot, and killing him before the killing blow lands saves the victim unhurt, so a teammate can rescue the target.

player_translation.summary: A cheap, fragile T1 hunter whose strike kills one class of target outright and can't touch anything else. Stalk the prey, pounce when the prompt shows a kill, and get clear before its friends turn on you.
as_user: You pick prey, not fights: the strike only locks onto the kind you can kill (soldiers, for a dog-like hunter), and every other unit under the cursor shows a crossed-out icon, so you never waste it on a tank.
The approach is the whole skill: one burst kills you, so you flank, wait behind cover and pounce on soldiers who are alone, reloading or looking away.
The strike is a short lunge with a brief wind-up; when it lands the victim dies whatever their health or armour, and you are left in the open for a moment.
One hunter per victim: if another hunter on your team has already claimed a target, your prompt greys out and you pick someone else.
as_target: If you are its prey, its approach is your warning: a distinct sound and a 'hunted' marker appear once a hunter commits to you, so you can turn, back into your teammates or shoot it; a single burst kills it.
The lunge has a readable tell and can be sidestepped, and damage or knockback during the wind-up cancels it.
If you are not its prey, it can't hurt you: shoot it to protect your soldiers.
In the threshold variant a notch on your health bar shows the execute line, so you can retreat or heal before you drop below it.
teammates: The hunted kind sticks together and covers each other's backs, which pushes hunters onto stragglers.
Vehicles and turrets make good bodyguards for infantry: the hunter can't hurt them, and they can kill it.
The hunter's team sets up the kill: pins, slows and scatters separate soldiers from their group, and in the threshold variant teammates wear targets down for the finisher.
A victim's teammates can rescue him by killing the hunter during its wind-up, before the strike lands.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse. On a card the strike is the signature ability on Q with a short cooldown, usable only while a valid target is within lunge reach; the cursor shows a kill icon or a crossed-out icon.
A unit whose only weapon is the strike, like the dog, keeps it on left mouse instead, and the cooldown becomes its recovery after each kill.
Middle mouse, the universal ping, on a lone soldier: 'straggler here'. The base pattern uses one counted key, leaving room at T1 for a dash.
feedback: Valid prey within reach glows in the hunter's colour on the hunter's screen; units of other kinds show a crossed-out icon.
A loud, distinct pounce sound and a wind-up pose readable from above (a crouch, then a leap arc on the ground).
A 'hunted' marker over the victim, seen by the victim and his teammates once a hunter commits, and a small claim icon that shows the one-hunter-per-victim rule.
A distinct execute icon in the kill feed, so players learn which unit killed them and why their health didn't matter.
Threshold variant: an execute notch drawn on every health bar while the hunter is on screen.
changes_from_rts: Red Alert's dog kills any soldier the moment it reaches him; here the victim gets a tell (wind-up and hunted marker) and a moment to react, because dying with no chance feels unfair to a player.
Red Alert's one-dog-per-victim rule stays, made visible as a claim icon, so two hunters can't double up on one soldier.
The prey should be a class players choose and can play around (infantry by default), never a hidden stat; the generator names it by class or target type.
In Red Alert soldiers don't shoot back at a dog by reflex; here every player can shoot the hunter, so its fragility becomes the main brake on it.
An outright kill on a unit someone paid for needs an answer at the same tier: the hunter's fragility, the tell and teammates; the threshold variant is the safer default for hunters of vehicles.

team_play.notes: The enemy answers it with unit choice (kinds it can't touch, or massed small arms) and by staying grouped; the hunter's team sets up stragglers for it; a victim's teammates can save him by killing the hunter before the strike lands.

notes: A target-kind filter on the strike and a kill that bypasses health and armour are simple rules in the damage system.
The lunge needs a short movement, a hit check at the end and a cancel on damage; the server must decide it, since latency makes 'it hit me from the front' disputes common for positional kills.
The one-hunter-per-victim claim, the hunted marker and the execute notch are UI and state work.
The threshold variant needs a damage check against current health and a cooldown reset on a kill.
An outright kill ignores price and tier, so the hunter hard-counters its prey whatever the prey cost.
Several hunters together can wipe a group of infantry faster than it can react; the claim rule and the wind-up are the brakes.
The threshold variant snowballs if a kill resets the cooldown in a crowded fight.
If the prey kind is too broad, the hunter has no real weakness.
The ranged variant takes away the approach that warns its prey, so its shot has to be slow and easy to see.
A death that ignored your health bar feels unexplained unless the wind-up, the hunted marker and the kill-feed icon make the cause plain.
Players must learn which kind each hunter can kill; the crossed-out icon and a class-coloured outline help.
The silent-kill variant hides information on purpose and should stay at high spice.

variants.name: Hunter of one kind
variants.summary: Kills one class outright (soldiers by default) and can't hit anything else; the base form.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert attack dog; Generals Colonel Burton's knife

variants.name: Finish the wounded
variants.summary: Works on any kind of target, but kills outright only once the target is below a threshold; above it the strike is an ordinary heavy hit. A kill readies the strike again at once.

adds_strengths.why: Finishes any target, of any kind, once it is worn below the threshold, and each kill readies the strike again.

adds_weaknesses.why: Against a healthy target the strike is only an ordinary hit, so it needs teammates to wear targets down first.

counters.why: Thick armour gives no safety once a target is below the threshold: it dies as surely as a light one.

countered_by.why: Healing and repair lift targets back above the threshold before the strike lands.
Wounded targets that can outrun it get out of reach before it strikes.

variants.name: Strike from behind
variants.summary: The kill depends on position: a strike to the target's back kills outright, one from the front is an ordinary hit.
variants.seen_in: Team Fortress 2 backstab; Halo beat down

adds_weaknesses.why: The strike works only on one kind of target and only up close; against anything else it is useless.
From the front its strike is an ordinary hit, so it must get behind a target that isn't watching.

variants.name: Committed takedown
variants.summary: The kill is a long finishing move that locks both units in place; if the attacker is killed before the blow lands, the victim walks away unhurt.

adds_weaknesses.why: The strike works only on one kind of target and only up close; against anything else it is useless.
Stands locked in a long finishing move, and if it dies before the blow lands, the victim survives.

variants.name: Silent kill
variants.summary: The kill raises no alarm: no death cry and no kill-feed line for the victim's team, so they learn of the loss late. The victim still sees what killed him.
variants.seen_in: Generals Colonel Burton's knife (no unit-lost alert); some Team Fortress 2 knives

adds_strengths.why: Its strike kills a soldier outright, whatever his health or armour.
Its kills raise no alarm, so the victim's team learns of the loss late and can't react.

variants.name: Kill from range
variants.summary: The kill is a shot fired from a distance instead of a close strike. It still works only on its prey, the shot takes time to arrive, and if the shooter dies before it lands, nothing happens.

adds_weaknesses.why: The shot works only on one kind of target; against anything else it is useless.
The shot is costly, takes time to arrive and does nothing if the shooter dies before it lands.

countered_by.why: Fast-firing rifles kill the fragile shooter while its shot is still in flight, so the shot does nothing.
Machines are not its prey, so they ignore the shot and can kill the shooter.

variants.name: Spawn from the victim
variants.summary: The kill hatches a pair of short-lived minions from the body that fight for the attacker until they expire.

adds_strengths.why: Its strike kills a soldier outright, whatever his health or armour.
Each kill leaves short-lived minions that keep fighting for it.
Its strike kills a soldier outright, whatever his health or armour.

adds_weaknesses.why: The strike works only on one kind of target and only up close; against anything else it is useless.

counters.why: Kills soldiers outright, so even the toughest infantry fall to a single strike.

countered_by.why: Fast-firing rifles in a group shoot the fragile hunter down before it reaches anyone.
Machines are not its prey, so they ignore the strike and can kill the hunter.

open_questions: Should an execute ever work on a player at full health (as the Red Alert dog does on any soldier), or only from behind or below a threshold?
Which kinds may be the prey: only infantry (the safe default), or vehicles too through the threshold variant?
Keep Red Alert's one-hunter-per-victim claim on every card, or only on the dog-like one-kind variant?
Does a silent kill (no kill-feed line for the victim's team) fit the game's readability rules at all?

shooter_fit.reason: A clear hunter-and-prey loop: a fragile pouncer that kills one class outright creates counter-picks, grouping and rescue plays, but it needs a wind-up and a tell so the victim gets a chance.
